title: Centre eases EPM norms to boost exporter participation
text:
Centre eases EPM norms to boost exporter participation

 New Delhi: The Centre on Wednesday announced modification in guidelines of the Rs 25,060-crore Export Promotion Mission (EPM) initiative to improve market access and expand exporters' participation in international trade events.

 Read E-Paper Story continues below. Go Ad Lite Story continues below. Go Ad Lite The Department of Commerce has amended the guidelines of four interventions under the Niryat Disha sub-scheme of EPM, which was approved by the Union Cabinet in November last year.
 With an outlay of Rs 25,060 crore for the period FY2025-26 to FY2030-31, the mission seeks to strengthen India's export competitiveness through targeted financial and non-financial support, with a particular focus on MSMEs, first-time exporters and under-represented regions.
 Under the amended guidelines the maximum eligible export turnover for availing airfare reimbursement for participation in Buyer-Seller Meets, trade fairs and trade delegations has been increased from Rs 75 lakh in the preceding year to Rs 50 crore.
 Story continues below. Go Ad Lite Story continues below. Go Ad Lite Airfare reimbursement has been enhanced to up to 95% for micro and small exporters and up to 80% for other eligible exporters.
 The mandatory membership period with Export Promotion Councils has been reduced from six months to three months, as per a statement issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 FIEO President SC Ralhan said the amendments seek to address three critical requirements of Indian exporters — access to international markets, affordability of quality certifications and the high cost of logistics. "By widening the eligibility criteria and enhancing the quantum and scope of assistance, the government has taken an important step towards ensuring that more MSMEs and emerging exporters can participate in global trade," he added.
